(per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao) This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief :
"....to issue a Writ of Habeas Corpus under Art.226 of the Constitution of India directing the respondents to release the Detenu i.e., Vincent Kavin S/o.Denny Vincent who is now detained in Central Prison, Cherlapally, Hyderabad District by setting aside the order of detention passed by the respondent No.2 vide proceedings Mary Vincent vs The State Of Telangana on 16 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11156100/
1 No.C.No.60/PDCELL/CCRB/RGM/2021, the Commissioner of Police,
Ramagundam, dated 26.09.2021, declaring the detention order as illegal, arbitrary,
discriminatory and unsustainable in the eye of law....
2.

entities.text: Mary Vincent vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed by the wife of detenu-Vincent Kavin challenging the order of detention dated 26.09.2021 made under Section 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers,
Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders,
Fake Documents Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime offenders and While Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act 1 of 1986).
3. Heard Sri Thomas Joseph Lloyd, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for home.
4. The order of detention is passed by referring to three crimes registered against the detenu under Sections 380 and 457 of Indian Penal Code (IPC), read with Section 511 IPC in one case.

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to learned counsel for the petitioner, last of the crimes was registered on 05.07.2021 and in all the three crimes, he was not even arrested by the police but notice under Section 41-A of Code of Criminal Procedure was issued.
While so, and after more than two months the order of detention was made referring to the very same three instances.
According to learned counsel, registration of three crimes does not warrant preventive detention.
5. We are not recording detailed reasons for our decision to allow this writ petition.

Having regard to the fact that similar issue was considered at length by the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.104 of 2021 and for the reasons assigned therein, allowed the writ petition setting aside the order of detention.
In that case order of detention was passed on account of involvement in six crimes registered under Sections 457 and 380 of IPC.

Paragraph Nos.11 and 12 of the order in W.P.No.104 of 2021 reads as under :
"A bare perusal of the impugned detention order clearly reveals that the detenu moved bail petition in Crime No.501 of 2020 and it was dismissed by the Court concerned.
The factual matrix of the case is that since the bail petition of the detenu was dismissed by the Court concerned, he continues to be in judicial custody.

Under these circumstances, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every possibility of the detenu moving another bail petition in Crime No.501 of 2020 and also in the remaining cases and in the event of his release on bail, there is every possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities which are detrimental to the public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an appropriate order of detention, is highly misplaced.
It is the bounden duty of the Police to inform the learned Public Prosecutor about the conduct of an accused and to handover the history-sheet of the accused.

The police are supposed to be vigilant in collecting the whole data against the detenu and to furnish the same to the Public Prosecutor/Additional Public Prosecutor to defeat the bail application/s of the Mary Vincent vs The State Of Telangana on 16 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11156100/
2 detenu.

entities.text: Mary Vincent vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the detenu has not been released from the judicial custody, the apprehension of his coming out from the prison and committing similar offences is misplaced.

It is appropriate to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rekha Vs State of Tamil Nadu1, wherein it is held as follows :
"Where a detention order is served on a person already in jail, there should be a real possibility of release of a person on bail who is already in custody, provided he has moved a bail application which is pending.

entities.text: Rekha Vs State of Tamil Nadu1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It follows logically that if no bail application is pending, then there is no likelihood of the person in custody being released on bail, and hence, the detention order will be illegal."
12.
Though the offences relied are more in number, they relate to lurking house-trespass and theft.
So, no inference of disturbance of public order can be drawn.
These cases can be tried under the normal criminal law.

Hence, there was no need for the detaining authority to pass the detention order."
6.
We are in respectful agreement with the view taken by the Division Bench.
Here also detention order is made referring to three crimes registered under Sections 457 and 380 of IPC and in one case Section 511 of IPC.
For the reasons assigned by the Division Bench in W.P.No.104 of 2021, the impugned detention order is not sustainable.

7. The Writ Petition is allowed and the respondents are directed to set the detenu namely Vincent Kavin S/o.Denny Vincent, Age : 36 yrs, Caste: Christian, Occu : Auto Driver, R/o.Q.No.T1-488,
8-Incline Colony, Godavarikhani, Peddapalli District, Aadhar No.260662816617 at liberty forthwith if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

P.NAVEEN RAO,J ______________________ Dr. G.RADHA RANI,J 16th February, 2022 Rds (2011) 5 SCC 244 Mary Vincent vs The State Of Telangana on 16 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11156100/
